specAnchors.text: describe the role of the placenta in the nutrition of the developing embryo

primer.text: A fetus cannot eat, breathe or excrete — yet it grows. Its delivery service is the placenta: a thin-walled, wide-surfaced exchange post where maternal and fetal blood run close enough to swap oxygen and nutrients for carbon dioxide and urea without ever mixing, while the umbilical cord links the trade route to the fetus.

modules.title: The Exchange Service Between Two Bloods
modules.opening: After implantation the placenta forms and becomes the fetus's lifeline: mother's blood and fetal blood flow close together but never mix, oxygen and nutrients cross toward the fetus while carbon dioxide and urea cross back, and the umbilical cord carries the exchange to the fetus.
keyPoints: After the embryo settles into the uterine lining, the placenta forms at that landing site.
The placenta is the exchange point where substances cross between maternal blood and fetal blood.
Oxygen and nutrients such as glucose, amino acids and vitamins pass to the fetus.
Carbon dioxide and urea pass from the fetus's blood to the mother.
The two blood supplies stay separate; the umbilical cord links fetus to placenta.

low.restatement: Food and oxygen in, waste out — through one organ, with the two bloods kept apart by a thin wall.
low.analogy: A border market where traders exchange goods across a counter without ever entering each other's country.
low.examPointer: Always state the direction of travel for each substance — the exam hint singles this out.

medium.restatement: The placenta earns its exchange title structurally: a large surface area and a thin wall shorten every diffusion path, and while some toxins slip past — nicotine, alcohol and virus particles included — it still blocks many pathogens from reaching the fetus.
medium.analogy: A sieve-like customs wall: fast trade for essentials, a partial filter for smugglers.
medium.examPointer: Mention large surface area and thin wall when asked why the placenta is efficient.

glossary.definition: The structure at the implantation site that exchanges substances between mother and fetus.
The cord connecting the fetus's blood supply to the placenta.
The settling of the embryo into the uterine lining, where the placenta forms.

figures.alt: Diagram of placenta showing a cross-section with labelled parts: placenta, placental membrane, villi, umbilical cord, foetus and mother's blood vessels.
